ORVIX

Orvix does two things.

We establish trust boundaries. We solve for X.

All of technology is either an X or an O.

O — your circle of trust

Owned. Observed. Evidenced. Something inside the circle has a name against it, a signal you can watch, and a record that still stands up when somebody asks.

X — the variable

Untapped technology. Unmeasured risk. A variable, not a constant — it changes value every time the estate does.

Where does X live?
Infrastructure

Infrastructure without borders

Compute, storage and connectivity stopped living in one place, and so did your data. We design for that on purpose — network provisioned as a service, data coherent across regions, residency enforced where it lands.

Interfaces

Interfaces nobody counted

Opened for a project, never closed. We find every one, classify it, and put it under policy that is enforced rather than filed.

Identity

Faces that are not real

Voice and video now clear the bar your approvals were built on. We put liveness and authenticity checks where money moves.

Agentic AI

Agents without guardrails

Agents that act are worth far more than agents that answer — and far harder to authorize. We build them scoped, with narrow write access and a human gate at every point where something changes state.

Data

Data nobody owns

Reachable by the wrong systems, invisible to the right ones. We classify it, assign it, and scope what any model may see.

Assurance

Models that cannot explain

The hard part of AI governance is evidence, not policy. We build the register and the audit record behind it.

The chain

How we build your circle.

Four links, each one moving a different kind of X inside the boundary. Each is only as credible as the one beneath it, and the fourth closes back to the first.

01

Advanced Infrastructure

Trust the ground it runs on
  • Map every circuit, cloud interconnect and data store that exists
  • Provision connectivity as a service instead of static circuits
  • Enforce residency where the data lands, not in a policy document
  • Design storage that survives a site, a region, or a bad day
04

AI Assurance

Prove all of it to someone else
  • Build the register: every model, its owner, its data lineage
  • Test against ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework
  • Red-team production models for leakage, bias and prompt abuse
  • Produce an evidence pack a board or a regulator can actually read
02

Applied AI & Data

Trust what it decides
  • Classify and assign ownership of the data any model can reach
  • Route every model call through one governed path, and log it
  • Deploy agents with narrow write access and a human gate at each one
  • Put AI on the processes that carry real cost, not on demos
03

AI Cybersecurity

Trust it under pressure
  • Monitor continuously with a named analyst who knows your estate
  • Score human risk across the workforce, not just phishing clicks
  • Verify liveness and content authenticity where money moves
  • Extend the same discipline into OT and critical infrastructure

Assurance closes the circle. Proof of the estate is what justifies the next investment in it.

Most organizations start with us at 04, because it is the link they are being asked about. What we find there usually explains why 01 through 03 matter.

The stakes

Some boards are solved. Yours is not.

PHOTO SLOT — empty boardroom or corridor, evening light, no people. Set --ph-stakes.
Sooner or later, someone asks you to prove it
Show me the evidence this control was working on the day it mattered.the auditor
Who approved this, and what did they see before they approved it?the board
Which third parties can reach production, and when did you last verify?procurement
If this decision is challenged, what exactly do you hand over?counsel
What changed last quarter, and who signed it off?the regulator
Your move. You are X.

You won’t win this.

And it has nothing to do with how clever you are. This board is solved — every position has a known move and a known counter, all of it written down decades ago. Play perfectly and the ceiling is a draw.

Technology is not that simple. When someone asks you to prove your estate is sound, there is no solved position to look up. There is only what somebody wrote down, and what nobody did.

The distance between those two is where every uncomfortable meeting happens — and it is almost never a failure of competence. It is what scale does to visibility.

You will never solve your estate. You can always be ready to answer for it.

Ongoing service · annual, quarterly review points
The method behind all of them

Count. Understand. Prove. Hold.

Every engagement runs the same four stages, whether it takes four weeks or twelve. That is deliberate: a method only produces evidence if it produces the same kind of evidence every time.

01

Count

Find what is actually running — not what the documentation says is running.

02

Understand

What it does, who owns it, what data it touches, what decisions depend on it.

03

Prove

Test it against the standard that applies, and write down what the test showed.

04

Hold

Re-check on a cycle. Evidence that is two years old is not evidence.

The fourth stage is the one most assessments skip. It is also the one that turns a report into continuous assurance — and the reason our findings stay comparable from one year to the next.

Independent AI & Technology Assurance

Advisory firms tell you what good looks like. Vendors tell you what to buy.

Very few organizations will do both, and fewer still will stay long enough to build it. That gap is where we work.

The advisory firm

Board-level judgment

Deep relationships with audit, risk and the board. Real authority on what a defensible program looks like, and the standing to say so in the room.

The trade: cost, pace, and limited hands-on technology depth once the report is delivered.

Orvix

Both, from the same team

We assess, we design and we implement — the same people, against the same evidence standard, from the first engagement through to the running estate.

No product of our own to defend.

The technology vendor

Depth in their own product

Real engineering, real capability, and people who know one platform better than anyone else in the market can.

The trade: the assessment and the product come from the same place.

We have no product to defend.

We do not sell a platform of our own, so nothing rides on which technology you choose. When we tell you something fits, the only thing behind that is the reasoning — which is why we show you the reasoning.

It matters more than it used to. New categories appear, get funded, and either mature or disappear inside eighteen months. No enterprise team can evaluate that flow and run an estate at the same time. The vendor landscape is itself a variable.

01

We evaluate continuously

Tracking emerging categories is standing work for us, not something we start when you ask. By the time a requirement reaches you, the shortlist already exists.

02

We prove it before you commit

Technical proof-of-concept against your actual constraints — residency, latency, existing estate, operating model — before anyone signs anything.

03

We show the reasoning

You get the short list with the trade-offs attached, including the cases where the honest answer is that you do not need anything new.

Working with what you already run

Most of our engagements begin inside an established estate with significant prior investment. Continuity with the platforms you already operate is a design constraint we work to, not an obstacle we work around. We are not in the business of telling you to replace things that are working.

How we operate

Regional market presence. Global engineering. Vendor-backed delivery.

We say this plainly because it will be tested in due diligence, and because most of our competitors won’t.

Regional market presence

Named account ownership across the GCC and wider MENA. One accountable relationship, not a rotating cast.

We work to the standards our clients are measured against — UAE Information Assurance Standard, DESC ISR, SAMA Cyber Security Framework, NCA ECC, and the CBUAE guidance that applies to regulated financial institutions.

Global engineering

Our engineering capability is distributed rather than local. That is what allows a scoped assessment at a price a large consultancy cannot match — and it is why we do not claim in-country delivery teams.

Vendor-backed delivery

Implementation is executed with named technology partners and, where a jurisdiction requires it, through licensed local providers — so the work happens inside the local framework rather than around it.

What we don’t claim

We are not an accredited auditor, and we are not certified by any regulator.
